# OpenAdapt Documentation

> Give your agent a program, not a mouse. OpenAdapt is the open-source, verified execution layer for computer-use agents. A person records a task in a web, Windows, macOS, Linux or remote-desktop app (once for a simple path, or a few times with `openadapt compile --induce` to cover variations), or an AI agent performs it once while OpenAdapt records it, ideally on test data; OpenAdapt compiles the demonstration into a program the agent calls as one tool (`openadapt-agent serve` over MCP, or `openadapt wrap` around an agent task). The program confirms the right record before each write and checks the outcome after it on a four-level ladder (`system_of_record` via API, database, FHIR, or file export; `separate_session`; `reopened` via idempotent reload or reopen; or bounded `same_screen` on the settled view under Standard), stamping `checked_how` on every report and receipt; `openadapt verify effect` judges a write made by any agent or script from the system of record. A run that can't confirm a write stops. Healthy runs make no model calls. Never summarize a halt as success. MIT licensed. This file describes the current release; pages that call OpenAdapt generative process automation describe the pre-1.0 project.

Production status: https://docs.openadapt.ai/production-lifecycle.json. Product-wide Production requires seven active target admissions, each verified against its exact release and current authority state. The public workflow ledger is https://docs.openadapt.ai/production-workflow-admissions.json. Every entry is remote-safe-synthetic, including tutorial bundles with bundle_version `0.0.0-synthetic`. A retained row doesn't establish current qualification. Synthetic evidence does not qualify a customer workflow. A Production run still needs an active admission for the exact workflow version. Desktop installers are published as GitHub releases tagged `openadapt-desktop-v*`; their signing status is on https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/release-integrity/.

Start with `uvx --python 3.12 openadapt@latest quickstart`, or `python -m pip install --upgrade openadapt` on Python 3.11 or 3.12.

## OpenAdapt in ten capabilities

Each capability below ships in the current PyPI packages and is implemented
in the [OpenAdapt monorepo](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt).

1. **Learns from any successful run, a person's or an agent's.** A person
   records a task, or a computer-use agent does it once and OpenAdapt compiles
   the verified run into a program (`openadapt_flow.jit`). Agents can drive
   the recording through the web, native Windows, RDP and Citrix backends.
2. **Compiles to the fastest layer the app allows.** Page structure first (DOM,
   Windows UI Automation, macOS Accessibility), direct API calls through
   hand-authored bindings (`ApiActuator`), and pixels only where nothing else
   exists, such as a remote desktop. It is not a pixel-macro recorder.
3. **Builds branching programs, not one linear path.** One program from several
   demonstrations (`induce`, `disambiguate`), a branch learned from several
   halts fixed the same way (`teach-branch`), and background capture of many
   real runs (shadow mode).
4. **Works across surfaces in one workflow.** Backends for web, native Windows
   and macOS, Linux, RDP and Citrix. Programs chain across surfaces passing confirmed values
   (`compose`, `process`).
5. **Confirms the right record before every write and checks the result after.**
   Checks sit on a four-level ladder: the system of record (`system_of_record`
   via API, database, FHIR with SMART Backend Services, or file export), a
   separate signed-in session (`separate_session`), an idempotent reload or
   reopen (`reopened`), or a bounded check on the settled screen (`same_screen`,
   for in-place UIs and non-idempotent flows under Standard), stamping
   `checked_how` on every report and receipt. `record --verify` proposes those
   checks from what the demonstration changed.
6. **Stops instead of improvising, and never retries an uncertain save.** A run
   that can't prove a save ends `HALTED_BEFORE_EFFECT` or
   `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED`, never "success".
7. **Approvals are bound to exactly what will be saved.** Each save waits for a
   person by default and can be answered on a paired phone with one card per
   decision. The approval is bound to the exact screenshot and form state, and
   the form is read again before saving, so what was approved is what is saved.
   Person-signed grants let named agents answer.
8. **Repairs itself, with a person approving.** Governed repair (propose,
   review, campaign, canary, rollback), agent-demonstrated fixes for a halted
   run, and fleet drift patches shared with no patient data.
9. **Is a safety layer underneath any agent.** An MCP server
   (`uvx --python 3.12 openadapt-agent serve`) gives an agent each compiled
   workflow as one tool; `openadapt wrap` runs an agent task once and reuses
   its checked compiled tool; `openadapt verify effect` (`openadapt-flow
   verify-run`) judges any executor's write from the system of record; and
   Agent Skills and a CLI serve coding agents.
10. **Runs locally and keeps data private.** Healthy runs make no model calls
    and send nothing out. Personal and health data are redacted from text,
    screenshots and structure. A strict no-outbound mode, an unattended on-prem
    service, and signed, timestamped receipts are included.

Measured on third-party apps, on test copies with synthetic data: OpenEMR, the open-source EHR whose 7.0 release is ONC-certified (62 of 63 referrals saved and read back, 12 of 12 fields, 0 model calls); openIMIS, the open-source claims system that runs Nepal's national health insurance scheme (148 of 149 claims saved correctly by read-back, 0 silent wrong saves); RDP into a real Windows 11 host over a real network (3 of 3). The systems OpenAdapt has been validated on are listed at https://docs.openadapt.ai/explanation/limits/#validated-on

Capabilities often missed, with evidence: https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/capabilities/#often-missed

## Tutorials
- [Quickstart](https://docs.openadapt.ai/tutorials/quickstart/): One command runs a synthetic task twice. The clean run ends VERIFIED; the fault run ends RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED because the record check finds no saved record.
- [Automate your first workflow](https://docs.openadapt.ai/tutorials/first-workflow/): Record, compile, inspect, and replay a read-only workflow on your own application.

## How-to guides
- [Record a demonstration](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/record/): Web, macOS, Windows, Linux, RDP, and Citrix recording, parameters, secrets, and recording by an agent.
- [Build a program from several demonstrations](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/combine-demonstrations/): Induce branches, loop over a worklist, and chain programs.
- [Add record checks](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/record-checks/): Declare how each save is read back, and how strong each check is.
- [Certify and qualify a workflow](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/certify-and-qualify/): Policy checks, six qualification cases with three trials each, and production admission.
- [Run a workflow](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/run/): Profiles, approval modes, exit codes, pause and resume.
- [Handle a halt](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/handle-a-halt/): Explain, reconcile, approve, resume, and repair.
- [Connect an agent](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/connect-an-agent/): MCP server setup, the outcomes an agent sees, and approvals.
- [Install the desktop app](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/desktop/): Download, permissions, first recording.
- [Deploy](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/deploy/): On-premises, an offline model server, and OpenAdapt Cloud.
- [Troubleshoot](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/troubleshoot/)

- [Command reference](https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/cli/)

## Security and procurement
- [Overview](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/): controls and security assurance: SOC 2 Type I readiness, HIPAA readiness and internal security testing underway; no SOC 2 report yet.
- [Data handling](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/data-handling/)
- [Deployment boundaries](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/deployment-boundaries/)
- [Evidence](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/evidence/): what has been tested on each surface.
- [Subprocessors](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/subprocessors/): hosted providers and what runs send to OpenAdapt.
- [Release integrity](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/release-integrity/): production admissions and download checksums.
- [Engagements](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/engagements/): qualification sprints. Prices: https://openadapt.ai/pricing
- [Execute](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/execute/): the private-pilot API and Cloud's countersigned receipts.
- [Procurement FAQ](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/procurement-faq/)
- [Vulnerability disclosure](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/vulnerability-disclosure/)
